strategy.summary: Reproduce PR #62813 on the buggy commit 27368892d374 by building pandas from source and running the PR's own updated tests. The transition is that maybe_convert_numeric raises ValueError('Integer out of range.') for integers >= 2^64 when coerce_numeric=False on the buggy revision, and returns object-dtype Python ints on the fixed revision. Test files come from the PR diff; no numeric value is checked separately.

pinned_because: python 3.11 is the reporter's observed version from the issue, not a documented constraint; any Python supported by the repo at that commit should also work

numpy is unbounded per the evidence (no documented constraint, no era entry); choose the numpy the buggy commit's pyproject build-system requires and record it, rather than the reporter's 1.24.1 which predates the buggy commit
pytest is unbounded and undocumented (only seen as 7.2.1 in issue #51295); use a current pytest compatible with the repo's test configuration
Cython must be installed before the no-build-isolation build because the extension modules in pandas/_libs are compiled from .pyx sources, which is why needs_build is true

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/dtypes/test_inference.py pandas/tests/tools/test_to_numeric.py pandas/tests/io/parser/common/test_ints.py -k 'convert_numeric_overflow or really_large or int64_overflow or outside_int64_uint64_range' -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: test_convert_numeric_overflow in pandas/tests/dtypes/test_inference.py (parametrized over four values including 1<<65 and -(1<<65), and coerce_numeric False/True); the enclosing class name is not stated in the evidence so select it with -k rather than a class path. Companion changes in test_to_numeric.py (test_really_large_scalar, test_really_large_in_arr, test_really_large_in_arr_consistent) and test_ints.py (test_int64_overflow and test_outside_int64_uint64_range, with python-engine xfail markers removed) are part of the same transition.
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit 27368892d374 with the PR test files applied: test_convert_numeric_overflow cases with coerce_numeric=False raise ValueError('Integer out of range.') from lib.maybe_convert_numeric and so error, the python-engine test_ints cases fail because their xfail markers were removed, and the to_numeric large-value tests fail on the expected-ValueError-versus-int change. On the fixed revision (PR #62813 applied): the same selection passes, with coerce_numeric=False producing object dtype holding Python ints and coerce_numeric=True producing float64.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np, pandas._libs.lib as lib; print(lib.maybe_convert_numeric(np.array([1<<65], dtype=object), set(), coerce_numeric=False))"

input_output_examples.input: CSV column value with rows: 42 and 18446744073709551616.5 read via pd.read_csv (default C engine, no dtype=)
input_output_examples.expected_output: numeric values with no str values left in the column; 18446744073709551616.5 is a float64 value per the maintainer and 42 stays numeric

input_output_examples.input: np.array([1 << 65], dtype=object) passed to lib.maybe_convert_numeric with coerce_numeric=False
input_output_examples.expected_output: object-dtype array holding the Python int 1<<65

risks: The reporter's environment (pandas 1.5.3, numpy 1.24.1) predates the buggy commit and must not be used as the reproduction target; the transition only holds on the buggy and fixed commits of the repo itself.
No platform or sanitiser dependence is evidenced: the behaviour is pure Python/Cython logic, so x86_64 Linux should reproduce it. Nothing in the evidence shows it needs a specific architecture.

The C and python read_csv engines take different paths; the read_csv evidence (issue #51295) used the default C engine, so the test_ints python-engine cases are the ones that exercise the python parser, and both should be included.
pyarrow engine and dtype={'value': 'float64'} workarounds must be avoided, since they change the path under test.
The editable build must be rebuilt when switching between buggy and fixed commits, otherwise stale Cython extensions could make the transition appear or disappear for the wrong reason.

The test class name is not in the evidence, so the test_command selects by -k rather than by class path; if a -k expression matches nothing the run passes vacuously, so check that tests were collected.
pytest and numpy versions are unbounded in the evidence; a much newer numpy could change overflow behaviour in object arrays, so pin the numpy the buggy commit's build requires.

oracle.reference_source: the PR's own test expectations in pandas/tests/dtypes/test_inference.py (object array of Python ints, or float array when coerce_numeric=True)
oracle.why: The expected values are Python ints compared by tm.assert_numpy_array_equal, which checks object and float arrays exactly, so no tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The coerce_numeric=False parametrizations call lib.maybe_convert_numeric on an object array containing 1<<65 or -(1<<65) (or their string forms). The buggy revision raises ValueError('Integer out of range.') from inside the call, before any assertion runs, so the test errors. The python-engine test_ints cases fail because their xfail markers were removed, and the to_numeric tests fail because they now expect int results where the buggy code raises.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision maybe_convert_numeric sets seen.overflow_ and returns an object array of Python ints for coerce_numeric=False, and float64 for coerce_numeric=True. Those arrays match the expected arrays exactly, so the selected tests pass.
